scope: The reviewed Oath default and Wallet Core 4.8.4 registry agree. The reference library reproduced the first address with the explicit path.
limitation: Covers the first ordinary BIP39 account. It does not establish every Trust Wallet app version, account index, token discovery result or smart account.

scope: The reviewed default matches the Wallet Core Bitcoin registry. Oath core also reproduced the published native SegWit address.
limitation: Other address types have separate core checks below. This is not a balance-discovery or funded-transfer test of Trust Wallet.

scope: Explicit-path and default-address derivation agree in Wallet Core. Public passphrase vectors and account isolation checks passed.
limitation: A matching address does not verify every TRC-20 contract, available TRX/resources or sending behavior.

scope: The released source exposes Trust Wallet and Phantom account conventions. The reference library produced different addresses for the same public fixture.
limitation: Use the matching account convention in Oath and compare its public address with the original wallet. An automatic match or full historical-account discovery was not tested.

scope: The MetaMask-documented default account branch and Oath’s first account align. Wallet Core reproduced the known first-account address.
limitation: Only ordinary phrase-derived EVM accounts are covered. Social-login recovery, hardware wallets, smart accounts and non-EVM/Snap accounts are outside this result.

account: Later or separately imported EVM account
result: A different account needs its own key or matching path
scope: The second account is distinct from the first. A reference-library test reproduced that second address from its individual public-fixture private key. Oath’s ordinary EVM private-key import is source reviewed.
limitation: This does not show that phrase import automatically restores all accounts. An individual key covers one account, not the other accounts derived from the phrase or a separately imported key.

scope: Released Oath core reproduced standard Electrum fixture addresses and key results, including receive and change branches.
limitation: This is Electrum’s own versioned seed format, not a BIP39 phrase merely used inside Electrum. No installed Electrum app or funded migration was exercised.

scope: Released Oath core reproduced SegWit fixture addresses and key results. The root differs from a BIP84 wallet even though both can produce bc1q addresses.
limitation: Do not infer the seed format from the address prefix alone. Multisig and Lightning state are outside this ordinary single-wallet result.

scope: The pinned fixture set includes old-format seed decoding and legacy address/key expectations, exercised by Oath core.
limitation: Old seeds do not support an extra seed extension in this implementation. An encrypted wallet-file password is not the same as a seed extension.

account: Standard or SegWit seed with extension
path: Same seed format and exact extension
result: Normalization and account isolation checks pass
scope: Oath core tests check extension normalization and distinct account results. Restoring the original wallet requires the same extension used to create it.
limitation: The website cannot recover a forgotten extension. Oath 5.0.2 excludes Electrum-derived wallets from its encrypted iCloud export; retain the original seed and extension backup privately.

scope: The core suite contains 2FA address/key and CJK normalization fixtures. Those are cryptographic checks, not proof that a migration preserves the original cosigning or security policy.
limitation: Do not use this row as a supported migration procedure. TrustedCoin interaction, original 2FA protection and custom multisig recovery were not validated end to end.

account: Hardware, smart accounts, social login, custom scripts
scope: A phrase or an ordinary private key is not a universal export of every account and authorization model.
limitation: No installed-app compatibility claim is made for hardware pairing, smart-account deployment/owners, social login, Snap accounts or custom scripts. Consult the original wallet’s recovery method.
